nodes.name: Kermes oak & oaks
nodes.desc: Oaks, including kermes oak recorded near the site, are common in the sub-Mediterranean woodland and drop acorns that many animals eat.

nodes.name: European hop-hornbeam
nodes.desc: A deciduous tree recorded in the area that grows with oaks in the lower broadleaf woodland.

nodes.name: Mountain grasslands
nodes.desc: Grasses of the subalpine meadows above about 1,500 m, where chamois graze in summer.

nodes.name: Mountain herbs
nodes.desc: Aromatic herbs such as mountain tea (Sideritis raeseri) grow here and have long been gathered by local healers.

nodes.name: Balkan chamois
nodes.desc: A rare goat-antelope of the gorge cliffs. It eats highland grasses and herbs in summer and moves lower in winter.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: A small woodland deer that browses leaves, shoots and herbs. It is recorded in the area.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for acorns, plants and invertebrates in the woods.

nodes.name: Wood mouse
nodes.desc: A small woodland rodent that eats seeds and fruit, and is food for foxes, martens and snakes.

nodes.name: Edible dormouse
nodes.desc: A tree-climbing rodent that eats nuts, seeds and fruit and is prey of foxes and martens.

nodes.name: Eurasian jay
nodes.desc: A woodland crow well known for gathering and caching acorns.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A versatile hunter of small mammals, birds and lizards, also eating fruit and carrion.

nodes.name: Beech marten
nodes.desc: A nocturnal mustelid that hunts rodents and birds and also eats fruit.

nodes.name: Balkan racer
nodes.desc: A fast, slender snake of the Balkans that hunts lizards and small mammals.

nodes.name: Short-toed snake eagle
nodes.desc: A raptor that specialises in catching snakes, and is recorded often around the gorge.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: An intelligent scavenger that feeds on carrion, including kills left by wolves.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter of wild ungulates such as chamois, roe deer and boar. It is listed among the large carnivores of the site.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Mostly a plant eater, taking acorns, berries and grasses, with meat and carrion in spring. The site is among its last southern European strongholds.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer sun drives growth on the sunny slopes and the high meadows.

nodes.name: Rain & snowmelt
nodes.desc: Rain and meltwater feed the woods and meadows, but the limestone drains fast so surface water is scarce.

nodes.name: Winter snow
nodes.desc: Snow covers the high meadows and pushes chamois down to lower forest in winter.

nodes.name: Limestone soil
nodes.desc: Thin soils over limestone, where water drains underground through caves and cracks.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
